description: compile() of bytes source where the first token is a number immediately followed by invalid-UTF-8 byte triggers an RPython AssertionError -> SIGABRT. Not statically checkable by this toolkit (lives in PEG-parser-generated C, not reviewable RPython source). Recorded for completeness/known-issues tracking only.

file: pypy/module/_struct (exact file TBD -- verify against release branch)
description: struct.unpack("u", ...) reads 4 bytes as a codepoint and passes it to unichr_as_utf8 without validating range (must be <= U+10FFFF, not a surrogate). Leaks as SystemError: unexpected internal exception. CPython removed the legacy 'u' format in 3.9; PyPy still accepts it unguarded.

file: pypy/module/_multibytecodec (exact file TBD -- verify against release branch)
description: codecs.getincrementalencoder(<multibyte codec>)().setstate(<negative int>) hands the state straight to rbigint.tobytes() without checking its signedness precondition. Leaks as SystemError. Affects all 12 multibyte encoders + their StreamWriter; decoders (tuple state) are unaffected. rbigint.tobytes is correctly guarded elsewhere (int.to_bytes raises OverflowError properly) -- setstate looks like the one unvalidated caller.

file: lib_pypy/_lzma.py (not present in main HEAD as cloned -- checkout/branch mismatch, see design doc note)
description: Two defects: (a) line ~562 assigns self._input_buffer = ffi.NONE after freeing it -- ffi.NONE does not exist (should be ffi.NULL per the very next line's check), so the assignment raises AttributeError, leaving a stale freed pointer. (b) line ~575's clear_input_buffer does an unlocked check-then-free of the same field that decompress() correctly locks elsewhere on the same class. Either defect alone or combined produces a double free / SIGABRT, reproduced deterministically and under threading.

file: pypy/module/_io/interp_textio.py (W_TextIOWrapper._dealloc_warn_w -- exact state TBD, see design doc note on version mismatch)
description: TextIOWrapper.detach() followed by ._dealloc_warn(None) segfaults. pypy#5123's fix (7bc330cce0f) added a w_raw-is-None guard to the analogous method in interp_bufferedio.py (the buffered layer) but never touched interp_textio.py's w_buffer field (the text layer) -- an incomplete fix applied to only one layer of the wrapper stack. Every other method on a detached TextIOWrapper raises ValueError cleanly; only this one is unguarded.

function: cyclic-finalizer collection after a caught MemoryError
description: Filling the heap with cyclic __del__ objects, CATCHING the resulting MemoryError, then gc.collect() segfaults (PyPy 6/6 at a 3072 MiB RLIMIT_AS; CPython 0/20 across five caps). The MemoryError is caught, so the program is in a state Python defines as recoverable. Distinguished from mere exhaustion by the ABSENCE of PyPy's clean 'out of memory: couldn't allocate the next arena' abort. Every line of the 14-line reproducer is load-bearing, including an `import weakref` that is never used -- substituting bytearrays or other imports does not restore it, so the threshold is in the GC heap's SHAPE, not its size. Needs an address-space limit; the reproducer sweeps a range because the window moves between machines and builds. Not statically checkable by this toolkit.

A no-argument multiprocessing.pool.ThreadPool() segfaults when the worker threads Pool.__init__ starts begin to fail against RLIMIT_AS. The intended outcome, which PyPy produces most of the time, is AttributeError: 'DummyProcess' object has no attribute 'terminate' from Pool.__init__'s own cleanup path; the bug is that the same situation sometimes segfaults instead. CPython raises cleanly under an identical limit and ballast (0/10). Highest-volume signature of the campaign (13 of 58 kept dirs in one fleet). The window is narrow and moves: adding a docstring to the reproducer shifted it by 150 MiB, so the shipped reproducer sweeps.

SECOND FACE of PYPY-FUZZ-001, same function, different call site. compile(b'0\xf5aa', ...) leaks an RPython KeyError as SystemError via the unicodedata table. Measured exhaustively over all 256 values of the byte following a digit, the outcome splits exactly along the UTF-8 validity classes: 0x80-0xC1 plus 0xE0/0xF0 abort (FUZZ-001), 0xF5-0xFF -- the bytes that could only encode above U+10FFFF -- leak here, everything else raises SyntaxError. Needs TWO further bytes after the lead byte, which is why b'0\xff' looked harmless as a negative control. Same producer as FUZZ-001 and FUZZ-012; fixing the producer would likely close all three. Not statically checkable by this toolkit.

glibc reports heap corruption ('free(): double free detected in tcache 2') at an address-space limit, where PyPy's own exhaustion abort is clean. Reproduced in TWO unrelated modules (functools, importlib.resources._common) in different fleet instances, which argues interpreter-level rather than module-specific. 8/8 at 3072 MiB; CPython clean at every cap. MECHANISM UNKNOWN and two hypotheses were tested and killed: a mishandled thread-bootstrap allocation (4000 threads under the limit with 0-3000 MiB ballast produced no corruption), and libmpdec through cffi (PyPy has no _decimal module at all). Two distinct windows exist (1536 and 3072 MiB); a four-point sweep finds one and misses the other.

SIGILL in the CHILD after fork() from a non-main thread, inside threading._after_fork walking a weakref set. Reached via concurrent multiprocessing.popen_fork.Popen() from worker threads, including re-running __init__ on an already-constructed Popen (the parent side of _launch succeeds even for a non-Process argument). The only SIGILL of the campaign across six fleets. PyPy 12/12 on the original script, 3/12 on the 109-line reduction -- it is a race, so the rate falls with size; CPython clean. An illegal instruction under an all-Python stack means an RPython ll_assert compiled to a trap or JIT code running in a state that no longer holds.

memoryview._pypy_raw_address() on a RELEASED view dereferences and segfaults; three lines, deterministic. Measured over the type's whole public surface one member per subprocess: 14 members raise 'ValueError: operation forbidden on released memoryview object', 3 (*contiguous) return without checking, and exactly one faults -- the one whose job is to hand back a raw pointer. 1 of 19. Also reachable via the idiomatic `with memoryview(...) as m:` form, since __exit__ releases. PyPy-only method, so there is no CPython differential; the argument is internal consistency. STATICALLY CHECKABLE: this is the sibling-guard shape the toolkit already scans for.

Formatting a SyntaxError produced from non-UTF-8 source leaks an RPython CheckError as SystemError. compile(b'\xff', b'\x80', 'exec') then traceback.format_exception(...) -- two bytes. BOTH halves must be invalid UTF-8: the source to produce the 'Non-UTF-8 code starting with ...' error whose message embeds the filename, and the filename for that embedding to go wrong. The compile is fine; the FORMATTING fails. Unhandled, the same input prints the filename as \Uffffefa0, which is not a codepoint -- the same out-of-range producer as FUZZ-001/008. DISTINCT from pypy-review-findings' PYPYR-0004 (verified side by side: OutOfRange vs CheckError, different guard, different entry). Adjacent to closed pypy#5111, which leaked the SAME CheckError and is FIXED on 7.3.23 -- this path is a door the fix did not reach.

_io.BufferedRWPair.__new__(_io.BufferedRWPair).closed segfaults; one line, deterministic. Every other type in the family answers that state with 'ValueError: I/O operation on uninitialized object' -- BufferedRandom, BufferedReader, BufferedWriter and TextIOWrapper all do. 1 of 8. `.closed` is the SINGLE ROOT: the seven faulting operations (.closed, iter(), list(), for-loop, .readlines(), .__enter__(), .isatty()) all consult it, while the nine that check the underlying object directly raise properly -- so it is a one-line-shaped fix. CPython raises RuntimeError. Adjacent to closed pypy#5140 and pypy#5126 (StringIO in an invalid state), BOTH FIXED on 7.3.23 -- the fix did not propagate to BufferedRWPair. STATICALLY CHECKABLE: sibling-guard shape.

_hashlib.HMAC.block_size passes a NULL ctx to OpenSSL's HMAC_CTX_get_md. HASH.__init__ sets self.ctx = ffi.NULL (twice -- a literally duplicated line), then py_digest_by_name raises on an unknown digest name, leaving a LIVE object with a NULL ctx; block_size calls HMAC_CTX_get_md(self.ctx) and only afterwards tests `if not md:`, so the check guards the RESULT of the call, too late. Needs __new__ plus an explicit __init__ to keep the reference. No CPython differential possible: CPython forbids constructing _hashlib.HMAC from Python at all. Mirror image of PYPY-FUZZ-004 in the same cffi-stdlib family -- that assigns a DANGLING pointer after freeing, this assigns NULL and dereferences it. Pure-Python source, so statically checkable.
